Classify a pedon under the Australian Soil Classification

Source: R/key-asc3.R
classify_asc3.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the Australian Soil Classification, 3rd edition (Isbell and the National Committee on Soil and Terrain 2021), following the online version with its errata. Experimental: this release keys the 15 orders (the key to soil orders) and the suborders of the Kurosols, Sodosols, Chromosols, Ferrosols, Dermosols, Kandosols and Vertosols (colour classes, and the Aquic Vertosols); the other suborders, great groups, subgroups and families follow. The name is the suborder's ("Red Chromosol") where one is assigned; rsg_or_order keeps the order.

Usage

classify_asc3(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("asc3")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "asc3", the deepest class in name, the order in rsg_or_order, the classes of each level in levels, the key trace, and provisional_because (classes before the assigned ones that could not be decided).

Details

The ASC is largely morphological. The diagnostics read field texture grades (field_texture, NCST Field Handbook codes; lab clay stands in and is undecided near the limits), the Australian horizon notation (A1, A2, B21t, Bhs, Bk ...; FAO/USDA designations are read by the role of each horizon), the boundary between the A and the B, pH (strongly acid: pHw below 5.5), ESP (sodic: 6 or more), subplasticity, free iron, grade of pedality, carbonates and the moisture of the horizons when described (soil_water_status: the Vertosols' cracks are not required in a solum described moist). From the site it reads drainage_class and tidal_inundation (Hydrosols, organic materials), surface_condition (a cracking surface, Vertosols) and designation_system ("asc" for the Australian notation). The choices where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "asc3", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Isbell, R.F. and the National Committee on Soil and Terrain (2021). The Australian Soil Classification, 3rd ed. CSIRO Publishing, Melbourne. Online version: www.soilscienceaustralia.org.au/asc.

See also

make_asc3_example, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_asc3(make_asc3_example("chromosols"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Red Chromosol"
